newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FOREKS GROUP H1 PROFIT UP, RAISES 1997 ESTIMATE.
newsitem.headline: FOREKS GROUP H1 PROFIT UP, RAISES 1997 ESTIMATE.

text.p: Forekspank said on Monday its group half-year net profit was 54.66 million kroons, including 48.9 million kroons profit by the bank.
Forekspank has also increased its group 1997 net profit forecast by 29.6 million kroons to 104.6 million kroons, it added in a statement.
Foreks Liising had a net profit of 3.4 million kroons, Foreks Vaartpaberid (Foreks Securities) 2.1 million kroons and Foreks Varahaldus (Asset Management) 257,000 kroons.
The group earned 141 million kroons in revenues, which is 88.6 percent of the total figure for last year.
Net interest revenues made up 25 percent of total revenues. It was down by three basis points due to a decrease in interest marginals and toughening competition in the loan market.
Its costs were 72.5 million kroons after six months, which is 71 percent of the total costs of last year.
"Here it can be concluded that revenues have grown higher than costs, which is also a reason for profit growth" the bank said.
The group 1997 profit estimate includes 96.4 million kroons for the bank and 8.2 million kroons from subsidiaries.
It said gave several reasons for the increase in the profit estimate, including successful operations of the bank and its subsidiaries.
It said higher than expected activity, a rise in local and neighbouring stock markets and a higher than estimated rise in its clients were also reasons for the revision of the forecast.
The group expects to grow assets at the same speed as the previous half year and they will amount to 2.7 billion kroons at the end of this year.
Its assets grew by 33 percent in six months to 1.93 billion kroons at the end of June.
Demand deposits rose by 6.5 percent to 851 million kroons while time deposits by 66 percent to 297 million kroons.
Its equity grew by 50 percent to 155.8 million kroons.
The growth in the loan portfolio was 70 percent to 649 million kroons, backed by a growing trend in the whole loan and leasing market.
